av_event.line_text: Not yet, no. Not yet. Hopefully, you know. Anyway, have you had the Somerset fella yet, Martin? Absolute legend.
av_event.what: His broad smile drops for a moment and he looks down and to the side, away from the screen, for about two seconds before 'Anyway', then looks back up with the smile back on.

text:
B: Hey, hello! Rhys, is it? Daniel. Nice to meet you, mate.
A: Hiya, yeah, Rhys. Nice to meet you.
B: Where are you calling from? I'm guessing not London, with that accent.
A: No, erm, Caerphilly. Just outside Cardiff. I work in Cardiff, though.
B: Cardiff, love it. I was there for a stag years ago, Six Nations weekend, absolute carnage. What do you do?
A: I'm a video editor. Senior editor and motion graphics, at an agency. Corporate films, social ads, bits that are sort of S4C-adjacent.
B: Oh nice, creative. I had you down as design or tech, to be fair, from the photo. What's the poster behind you?
A: Oh, it's a Polish film poster. Vintage. I sort of collect them. The Polish designers in the sixties did these amazing posters for Western films, they'd just ignore what the film was actually about and do something completely mad. Sorry, I get a bit...
B: No, mate, that's cool. I've got a Spurs stadium sketch, so you've out-classed me there.
A: Ha. What do you do, then?
B: Solicitor. Commercial property, in the City. Leases, buying and selling buildings. Sounds dull, but honestly the clients are good fun. I'm senior associate, so hopefully partner in the next couple of years, fingers crossed.
A: Partner, that's, yeah. That's the big one.
B: It's the big one. Long hours, though. You must do long hours in the edit, deadlines and that?
A: Fifty, fifty-five some weeks. Erm, the deadlines, yeah. I'm on a pint of coffee by nine.
B: Ha, same, completion week I'm basically running on flat whites.
A: I saw the bike wheel in your photo, by the way. Made me feel guilty. I bought a road bike in lockdown and it's just in the garage.
B: Honestly, that's Hannah's, my wife's. I'm more of a runner. Wandsworth Common three times a week, Garmin, the whole thing. Got a parkrun PB a couple of weeks ago, actually, twenty-one something.
A: That's quick. I walk the dog up Caerphilly Mountain, that's my cardio.
B: Counts, mate. Hills count.
A: That's what I tell myself.
B: Are you a city break person? You look like a city break person.
A: Erm, yeah, actually. Copenhagen, Lisbon, Berlin. My wife plans it all, I just sort of get anxious at the airport and then eat.
B: No way, we've done Lisbon and Copenhagen. In Copenhagen there was this place with a waiting list of months, and I basically rang every day till they had a cancellation. Best meal of my life.
A: Oh, which one? Food's sort of my thing. I do these big weekend projects, ramen broth, slow-cooked lamb. The kitchen looks like a bomb's gone off after.
B: I'll have to look it up, Hannah'll know the name. Ramen from scratch, though, that's commitment.
A: It's twelve hours of bones on the hob. Ffion just opens all the windows. Erm, do you cook?
B: Roast, chilli, steak with peppercorn sauce. I can do a roast for eight, that's my party trick. But mostly I book the table. I keep a list of all the new openings. There's a small-plates place in Clapham, I got in the first week.
A: That's a good list to have. There's a few in Cardiff now doing tasting menus. I went to one for our anniversary and posted it all over Instagram, very embarrassing.
B: Nothing embarrassing about that, mate. If you don't post it, did it even happen?
A: Ha. Yeah, no, that's fair. Erm, have you and Hannah got kids, or...?
B: Not yet, no. Not yet. Hopefully, you know. Anyway, have you had the Somerset fella yet, Martin? Absolute legend.
A: Not yet. I had Lisa first, she was lovely. Dead friendly.
